text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT: Prod alert - high 5xx rate on inference-api. Canary rollout for encoder-service (model-encoder-v3) showing CrashLoopBackOff + HPA oscillation. Pager triggered. Severity: P1. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/r/enc/errors

maria: I'm on it, grabbing logs and kube state.

lee: seeing ~600 502s/min, canary pods on k8s-gpu-pool-2 are CrashLoopBackOff, restart loop every ~30s.

maria: quick kube snapshot:
```
$ kubectl get pods -n prod -l app=encoder -o wide
NAME                                 READY   STATUS             RESTARTS   AGE   NODE
encoder-canary-5f6d7c8b7f-abcde      0/1     CrashLoopBackOff   12         8m   gpu-node-23
encoder-canary-5f6d7c8b7f-fghij      0/1     CrashLoopBackOff   11         7m   gpu-node-24
encoder-stable-88c9d9c7b-xyz12       1/1     Running            0          2d   gpu-node-07
```

devon: HPA report shows minReplicas=0 and target CPU 80%. autoscaler allowed scale-to-zero between canary rollouts which caused burst startup and OOMs on warmup.
```
$ kubectl describe hpa encoder -n prod
MinReplicas: 0
MaxReplicas: 10
TargetCPUUtilizationPercentage: 80
CurrentReplicas: 0
DesiredReplicas: 6
```

jonathan: fwiw last deploy changed readinessProbe timeout from 5s -> 1s in encoder deployment (manifest change in canary job). that makes pods fail readiness on heavy init. suspect readiness flapping -> evictions.

sarah: customer-impact check: CS metrics show ~3% requests getting 503/504s, concentrated on long-generation customers (enterprise A, enterprise B). SLA risk. paging + customer comms in progress.

maria: immediate mitigations: 1) flip feature flag to stop routing traffic to encoder-v3 canary 2) scale encoder-stable up and scale canary down 3) patch HPA minReplicas to >=2 to avoid scale-to-zero during stabilizing. @devon can you flip the flag?

devon: flipping flag `use_encoder_v3` -> false in FF service now. will post when done.

infra-bot: Feature flag `use_encoder_v3` set to false by devon at 12:14:22 UTC. Change propagated to 91% of edge nodes in 14s.

lee: scaling commands applied:
```
kubectl scale deploy encoder-stable -n prod --replicas=6
kubectl scale deploy encoder-canary -n prod --replicas=0
```

jonathan: patching HPA minReplicas:
```
kubectl patch hpa encoder -n prod --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/minReplicas","value":2}]'
```

maria: also rolling canary image back to v2 for safety: `kubectl set image deploy/encoder-canary encoder=redwood/encoder:v2 --record`

sarah: CS update ready. sending interim notice to affected customers: we identified a rollout readiness/probe regression causing instability; mitigation underway, will follow up in 15m with status.

devon: monitoring: error rate trending back to baseline ~5m after flag flip and scale. no more CrashLoopBackOffs showing. CPU still jittery but stable.

maria: good. documenting timeline in incident doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/incidents/4123456789-encoder-canary. Runbook: runbooks/deploy-canary-rollback.md.

maria: handing off active monitoring to @oncall-next for the next 2h. I'll remain available for escalation. TODOs for oncall-next: watch SLOs, ensure HPA stable, confirm no regressions in canary logs, and coordinate with CS on postmortem.

oncall-next: acknowledged, taking over monitoring. will escalate if error rate > baseline + 0.5% or if any canary pods reappear in CrashLoopBackOff. :thumbsup:
